A [[Trandoshan]] [[Gender|male]] operated as a member of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] during the [[New Republic era|era]] of the [[New Republic]]. In [[9 ABY]], the '''bounty hunter''' was recruited by [[Greef Karga]] to steal a [[force-sensitive]] [[Din Grogu|child]] from [[Din Djarin|the Mandalorian]]. He was ambushed by a [[Nevarro reptavian|native reptavian]], who plucked him from the ground and [[Death|killed]] him.

==Biography==
{{Quote|It seems we've both provided a security detail.|Greef Karga|<ref name="Chapter 7" />}}
In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date" /> the [[bounty hunter]] was a<ref name="Chapter 7" /> loyal<ref name="PostGCW">{{EncyclopediaCite|Post-Galactic Civil War and the Mandalorian}}</ref> member of the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]]. He was recruited by the Guild [[agent]] [[Greef Karga]] on [[Nevarro]] to join his "security detail," alongside a [[Unidentified human bounty hunter (Nevarro)|human]] and a [[Unidentified Nikto bounty hunter|Nikto]]. Karga planned to confront the [[Mandalorian]] [[bounty]] hunter [[Din Djarin]], who was in possession of a [[Force-sensitive]] [[Din Grogu|child]] that an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] had tapped the Guild to capture.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

The Trandoshan and his two colleagues joined Karga in meeting Djarin in the [[lava fields]] on Nevarro. Djarin arrived on his [[starship]], the ''[[Razor Crest]]'', and approached the four with his own team, the ex-[[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] and the [[Ugnaught]] [[Kuiil]], riding [[blurrg]]s. Karga began by acknowledging both their security details and inspected the Child.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

[[File:Trandoshan_Carried_Away_The_Mandalorian.png|thumb|left|215px|The Trandoshan was caught by a Nevarro Reptavian.]]
The two parties then traveled across the lava fields towards the city and set up camp for the night. That night, the group sat by the fire and Djarin and Karga discussed plans to kill the supposed [[The Client|leader]] of the Imperial forces in the city. As Karga said this, the camp was attacked by [[Nevarro reptavian|native reptavians]]. The bounty hunters fended them off as they tried to seize the blurrgs, taking one away in the process.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

As a moment of silence ensued, the Trandoshan looked around, only to be taken by surprise by one of the creatures, who carried him away<ref name="Chapter 7" /> and [[Death|killed]] him<ref name="PostGCW" /> as Karga and the rest of the group shot at it.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

==Equipment==
The Trandoshan bounty hunter wore a tattered [[Color|brown]] and white outfit with writing at the end of his right sleeve. He wore a gray bowl-shaped [[helmet]], a [[necklace]] decorated with [[Tooth|teeth]], and a device on the right side of his abdomen. The Trandoshan wielded a [[vibro-ax]] and a [[blaster]].<ref name="Chapter 7" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|They mentioned using a Trandoshan again, and there had been a lot of exploration of that race in Season 1. Well, let's give it a helmet and see how it looks with just its weird toothy reptilian grin showing.|Brian Matyas|<ref name="Art of Mando">[[The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian (Season One)|''The Art of Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One]]</ref>}}
[[File:TrandoshanBH-concept-MandoArt.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Concept art for the Trandoshan by Brian Matyas.]]
The Trandoshan bounty hunter first appeared in "[[Chapter 7: The Reckoning]],"<ref name="Chapter 7" /> the seventh episode of [[Jon Favreau]]'s live-action [[Disney+]] series the ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' which was directed by [[Deborah Chow]] and released on [[December 18]], [[2019]].<ref name="S1 Companion">{{InsiderCite|201|Star Wars: The Mandalorian Season One Companion|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'' Season One Companion}}</ref> The character was played by an unspecified extra.<ref name="Chapter 7" /> In making concept art of the bounty hunter, artist [[Brian Matyas]] was advised about using a Trandoshan, and chose to explore putting a helmet on the alien to only show its mouth. Art director [[Doug Chiang]] added that it helped give the character a distinct look from the other bounty hunters.<ref name="Art of Mando" />
